To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we describe novel variants in BLOC 1S3 gene, in three consanguineous HPS‐8 families, and that we report a mild form of HPS‐ 8.
three new variants in BLOC 1S3 gene are reported in patients with HPS‐7.
we describe three new HPS patients carrying pathogenic variants in the BLC1S3 gene.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of novel variants in the HPS‐8 gene in a mild HPS form and the description of lymphocyte‐predominated Hodgkin lymphoma associated with this form.
the description of three new variants in BLOCI1S3, the gene coding for BLOC‐1 subunit B3 (B3C) that is involved in the biogenesis of lysosomal organelles.
the identification of novel variants in the BLOCS1S3 gene and the clinical description of a new HPS‐8 family.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
HPS‐8, HPS‐7, HPS‐9 and HPS‐11 are the same disorder, which should be renamed BLOC‐1 HPS.
the clinical spectrum of HPS‐1 to HPS‐8, HPS‐10, and HPS‐11 is very wide and the same symptoms could be associated with different forms, even with the same form.
HPS‐8 patients have a moderate form of HPS with a bleeding diathesis as the main symptom.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
BLOC‐1 is a critical subunit of a complex that is essential to the function of other BLOC‐1 subunits.
BLOC1S8 is the eighth gene involved in HPS, and that HPS‐8 has a milder clinical presentation.
HPS‐8 should be considered in the differential diagnosis of patients presenting a mild oculocutaneously albinism with or without bleeding diathesis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
BLOC1S8 should be included in the diagnostic work‐up for HPS.
BLOC1S8 variants should be considered as a possible cause of HPS in patients with oculocutaneus albinism and platelet dense granule anomalies.

BLOC‐1 subunit variants are responsible for the milder HPS forms, which is consistent with the hypothesis that BLOC‐3 and BLOC‐1 complexes are functionally related and that the BLOC‐1/BLOC‐3 complexes have an essential role in melanosome maturation and platelet dense granule formation.
